summary: Yes, spend moe's last check on this, but not as written. Rebase it onto the bucket-gate build (hyp/.../s5-copy-safe-bucket-gate). Keep B256 byte-identical to that build, and put the new NMAX=32 kernel at B128 behind the same >=1.02x graph-replay selector against Marlin, instead of forcing it on. One check then either beats 1.3744 with a landable build or re-measures the pending land candidate, and the prepare log still shows the ring-depth effect.
justification: MECHANISM: plausible for the routing it was derived from, overstated for the judged one. w13 is 8192x4096 NVFP4, about 18.9 MB per expert, and a whole expert is about 28.3 MB. The prepare zipf a=0.3 routing touches all 32 local experts, about 604 MB of w13, which s5 moves in 303-308 us at about 2.0 TB/s. With 132 CTAs x 37 KB in flight, that matches Little's law at the about 2.5 us loaded latency implied by the bf16 LESSONS number (64 KB/CTA -> 3.3 TB/s). So 'capped by bytes in flight' is reasonable there, and STAGES=10 (92 KB) could plausibly reach about 3 TB/s. JUDGED REGIME: reference.py's floor counts touched experts. 101.3 us x 4.8 TB/s gives about 17 touched experts at bs=128, and about 18 at bs=256. The judge's Student-t popularity plus the busiest-GPU rotation concentrates routes. The judged s5 w13 row of 238.4 us is therefore about 321 MB at only about 1.35 TB/s, and the pair is about 484 MB in 349 us, about 1.39 TB/s, against Marlin's 1.58 TB/s (306 us). In the scored regime a second limiter is visible: tail imbalance (about 17 chunks x 64 tiles = about 1088 items over 132 CTAs is about 8.2 rounds), and per-expert route counts large enough to need N32/N64/N128 consumers. A deeper ring cannot fix either. WEAKEST LINK: flat time across N is equally consistent with a dequant-bound consumer, since dequant work scales with weight bytes, not N. The s3 variant-B null only rules out a gain from overlapping MMA with dequant, not dequant ALU throughput. Also, '7.5 routes per local expert' is the prepare routing. At about 17 touched experts and about 14 routes per expert on average with a heavy tail, the hot experts exceed 32 routes, so NMAX=32 splits them and re-streams 18.9 MB of w13 (plus 9.4 MB of w2) per extra chunk. In the judged regime that cuts directly into the gain, and the prepare zipf a=0.3 routing will never trigger it. TARGETS: w13 <=170 / w2 <=80 needs 1.9-2.0 TB/s on the judged bytes. That is reachable only if the ring is really the limit and re-streaming stays below about 10%. A pair of about 280-300 us (beating Marlin's 306 by a little) is the realistic upper outcome, not a sure one. Upside if it lands: bs=128 from 314 to about 285-290 us scored, about +1.4-1.6% on the headline (about 1.39-1.40). Shape mapping is consistent with TASK.md: verify_16 = bs128 is the only scored B128 shape, and the skewed-128 test is a correctness test only. Q1, BEST USE OF THE LAST CHECK: yes among the queued moe items. B128 is the only scored verify bucket still on Marlin, the change isolates one variable (ring depth via slab size), and its prepare A/B against the unchanged s5 kernel is interleaved in-process. s6-per-kernel-bucket-mix is weaker: the forced profile shows wgmma losing both cells at B128 (238.4+gather vs Marlin call 1, 110.9 vs Marlin call 2, against a Marlin pair of 306), so it can only reshuffle a known loss. b256-n64-deep-ring widens a bucket that already wins, with the same mechanism risk and a smaller relative gap. But only the rebased/gated form makes the check landable. The forced form puts a probable loser on bs=128 (s5-forced scored 364.8 vs 314.3 Marlin), so the headline cannot be promoted. Its only extra yield, judged kernel rows for the new kernel, matters less now: the judged-vs-prepare gap is calibrated (selector predicted direction correctly at B128 0.80x and B256 1.05x), and the forced rows already exist for s5. Q2, BASE ON BUCKET-GATE: yes. FINDINGS says that build is code-identical to s5-forced apart from the selector, and judged B256 rows match (239.2+119.0+4.8 vs 271.0+126.1+4.8; scored 404.85 vs 404.67). Basing there keeps the B256 win, makes bs=256 an in-run control against job 7be125e9 (404.85 us), and lets M3 (the selector) merge into this stage, which saves a future check.
confounders: cuda-nvfp4-wgmma-rega-grouped-s5-copy-safe-bucket-gate / s5-forced (parent kernel, not landed): every B128 comparison is against s5's wg_kernel or Marlin, so read deltas against the bucket-gate job 7be125e9 (bs=128 scored 314.26, Marlin path) and the forced job d4ad4f31 (wg rows 238.4/110.9), never against BEST.json's master row alone.

marlin-block-m-two-smaller-on-postnorm (landed, block_size_m two candidates down at T>=128): sets Marlin's bsm 16 at bs=128, which is the incumbent the B128 selector must beat. If that pick were different, the Marlin bar (306 us judged) would move and so would the gate decision. No interaction with the wgmma kernel itself, which aligns at block 16 on its own.

align-parallel-per-expert-verify (landed, align at T>32): the wgmma path uses master's moe_align_block_size at block 16, not this align, but the gate compares full paths. Align cost (2.5-4 us) differs between the two paths and is inside the selector's 'full path' timing, so it is correctly included. Not a confounder for the kernel rows.
post-expert-norm / w2-atomic-add / triton-map-align (landed, all T<128 or downstream norm unchanged): untouched by this change. The norm runs identically after either path. No confound.
interference: No companion. Moe has one check left, so a companion is unaffordable, and none is needed if the build is rebased as recommended. The prepare log then holds the clean A/B the result needs: s5 kernel vs NMAX=32 vs Marlin at T=128, interleaved, cold L2, 41 reps, empty-graph baseline subtracted, on the same state. That separates 'deeper ring helps' from 'judge drift', and the bs=256 row (byte-identical to bucket-gate) is the in-run drift control. Two additions make one run interpretable either way. (1) The selector and the timing print must include a judge-like heavy-tailed routing: Student-t per-expert popularity plus busiest-GPU rotation, as reference.generate_input does, synthesized in prepare, never taken from inputs. Print touched experts, max routes per expert, chunk count and re-streamed weight bytes. Gate on the WORSE ratio of zipf a=0.3 and that routing, because zipf a=0.3 touches all 32 experts at about 7.5 routes each and never exercises NMAX=32's re-streaming, which the judge's about-17-touched-expert routing will. (2) Print achieved TB/s per kernel (touched-expert bytes / time) for s5 and NMAX=32 at both routings. If NMAX=32 is flat vs s5 at the all-touched routing, the ring is not the limiter, and the consumer (dequant + wgmma_wait<0>) is the next stage's target, not the b256-n64 sibling.
open_questions: Rebase detail: confirm with the user that basing on the unlanded bucket-gate branch is acceptable while its landing is pending. If bucket-gate is then landed, this result restacks with no conflict, because B256 is byte-identical.

If the user insists on the forced form (to get judged NMAX=32 rows), accept that bs=128 will likely score worse than 314 us and the run is not promotable. Then the run is worth the check only as a rewrite-stage measurement.

Consider NMAX=64 / STAGES=7 at B128 instead of NMAX=32 / STAGES=10. With about 17 touched experts and a heavy tail, the 2-block chunk cut may re-stream more weight than the deeper ring saves. A prepare print of max-routes-per-expert under the judge-like routing decides this, and building both and letting the selector pick is cheap (two more template instantiations).

Build time: two extra instantiations (w13/w2 at NMAX=32) plus the selector add perhaps 20-40 s to s5's 37.5 s. That is well under WG_SETUP_BUDGET_S=200, but the build-failure fallback must leave B128 on Marlin (not s5) and B256 on the bucket-gate decision.

STAGES=10 is not a power of two: n % STAGES and (n / STAGES) & 1 stay correct, but recheck any code that assumed STAGES=4 (bit masks, unrolled init loops, barrier array sizing tied to 2*STAGES in static smem).
